q: The copper currency for a long time consisted almost entirely of Dutch “duits” or “challis,” which were exported for the eastern currency and circulated freely all along the western coast.
1912, R.P. Jackson, “The Dominions, Emblems, and Coins of the South Indian Dynasties”, in British Numismatic Journal, page 319:

e: Borrowed from Afrikaans duiker (literally “diver”), from Dutch duiker, from Middle Dutch dukere. Piecewise doublet of ducker.
q: Next day she rose early, and went out with the gun and killed a duiker on the edge of the Big Tobacco Land (where her father had grown tobacco during his season's phase of believing in it).
1952, Doris Lessing, Martha Quest, Panther, published 1974, page 65:

e: From the Hanyu Pinyin romanization of Mandarin 對聯 /对联 (duìlián).
